title: P1 ownership-oracle copy and release-gated consumer check
question: How do P1 checks consume the ownership oracle, and does P1 extend the blocking consumer check to the release workflow?

options.text: Byte copy of target-map.json in tests/Arch/Fixtures with a recorded sha256, plus the consumer check in release.yml validate (chosen)
Tests read plans/<ID>/artifacts/inventory/target-map.json directly; release gating left to P4

context: Owner-agreed deviations from the literal P1 text (brief M10, M13). P1#design-inputs names artifacts/inventory/target-map.json as the oracle; a repository test reading the plan directory breaks when plan.py archive moves it to plans/archive/ and in split archives. Phase scope.include names only the tests workflow and bin/consumer-fixture.sh, while release-gate condition 9 requires that a tag release cannot bypass the blocking consumer check.
decision: A — Byte copy of target-map.json in tests/Arch/Fixtures with a recorded sha256, plus the consumer check in release.yml validate (chosen)
rationale: Owner agreed both points in the P1 design session (brief M13).
consequences: P2/P3 changes to the type map re-copy the generated file and update the sha in the same commit.
A tag release fails when Packagist is unreachable (consumer-fixture exit 3), never silently green.

evidence.note: Owner answers in the P1 design session.
